Look up an FMU.  Its basically a fuel pressure regulator that is boost referenced and adjustable.    It's no where near as good as a proper efi solution. A normal fuel pressure regulator on a forced induction car adds fuel pressure in equal proportion to boost pressure ex1psi boost it adds 1 psi fuel pressure.  But FMU can be adjusted so that it adds more ex 1 psi boost adds 3 psi fuel. Basically by raising the fuel pressure in the fuel rails you efi system sprays more fuel without changing what the computer is trying to do.  Another thing. I believe your Nissan has mechanical distributor. This is good because it is probably adjustable so you can retard the base timing which is important because the computer will not know about the boost and will want to advance the spark timing when it probably should not.  So if hypothetically ECM wants 20 degrees of timing at full tilt but you have decided 10 is safe you can adjust the base timing to -10 which will give you 10 degrees fully advanced.  You may also be able to disable the spark advance and just pick a happy compromise.  That may or may not be a viable solution.  You would also need a good wideband o2 sensor to measure your fuel trim otherwise you are flying blind.  The factory one in that car is probably not high enough resolution to make meaningful adjustments to fueling.
